title: Proactive locality-aware hedging and shedding for multi-region routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe transient latency spikes and capacity hotspots in specific GPU pools and regions. Current steering uses simple latency-percentile thresholds and hard geo-pinning; during capacity exhaustion this causes cascading failures and uneven shedding that breaches SLOs.

Goal: Implement a proactive routing policy that combines fast hedging (parallel speculative requests), locality-weighted scoring, and capacity-aware shedpoints so that: (1) p95/p99 SLOs are maintained for global customers, (2) local region preference is respected when healthy, (3) overload is gracefully degraded with predictable customer impact, and (4) circuit breakers trigger before hard failures.

High-level approach: Build a "Locality Hedging and Shedding" controller in the request director that computes a real-time score per candidate region/pool and decides: route primary -> optionally hedge to a secondary -> apply soft-pin or shedpoint when capacity headroom is low. The controller integrates with existing circuit-breaker service, capacity telemetry, and routing heuristics.

Key behavioral primitives introduced in this ticket: 1) locality score decay (soft-pin): a tunable decay function that keeps requests in a preferred region for short windows even after metric degradation, 2) hedge window: a short speculative parallel request to a warm warm-standby region when p95 latency is predicted to breach SLO, 3) shedpoints: pre-computed capacity thresholds that start selective shedding by traffic class (best-effort vs core) rather than global deny, 4) capacity headroom scoring: a combined metric mapping GPU utilization, queue length, and token-rate to a headroom [0..1] used by the routing score.

We prioritize predictable customer impact: shedpoints expose policy (which customers / routes are shed first) and integrate with billing/SLAs so alerting and tickets can be automated when shedding occurs.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes region scores every 100ms and returns route decision within 5ms additional latency
Add hedging: when predicted p95 breach probability > 0.2, send speculative request to one secondary region with cancellation on first response
Soft-pin decay retains regional affinity for at least 10s after small transient latency spikes (configurable), preventing noisy flips
Shedding is selective by route label: non-critical routes are shed first and documented in policy UI
Circuit-breaker trips and prevents hedging to a region that has >20% recent error-rate or sustained queue depth above threshold
Load test shows 30% fewer p99 SLO violations under synthetic burst compared to current steering config
Telemetry surfaced: per-route routing decisions, headroom, hedge counts, shed events, and circuit-breaker status appear in runtime-2.1 dashboard
design_decisions: Use an additive scoring model: score = locality_boost * L - latency_penalty * Z(latency) + headroom_weight * headroom_score - error_penalty * error_rate
Limit hedges to a single secondary to bound costs and avoid amplification; hedges are cancellable once first token arrives
Implement soft-pinning (locality decay) rather than hard pins to reduce thrash during transient noise
Expose shedpoints as named policy levels (SHEDP-1 .. SHEDP-4) to make postmortem analysis easier
Integrate with circuit-breaker service to mark regions as "hedge-disabled" rather than fully blacklisting, enabling gradual recovery
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: enable controller for 5% of traffic for internal customers with verbose logging, 2) Observe for 48h, track p95/p99 and shed events, 3) Gradually expand to 25% then 60% with home-region preference preserved, 4) Full rollout once we hit <10% increase in cost and p99 regressions are eliminated. Rollout toggles per-customer and per-route available in Console. Backout: toggle to previous steering policy immediately if p99 degrades >20% vs baseline.
metrics_and_dashboards: Shed_events by policy level and routes affected
p50/p95/p99 latency with routing decision label (local / hedge / failover)
Cost delta: hedging extra tokens vs SLO improvements
tests: Unit tests for scoring function with synthetic latency/headroom inputs
Integration test: simulated region A latency spike -> expect single-hedge to region B and cancellation after first-byte
Chaos test: continuous queue depth increase in region C should cause progressive shedding and ultimately a circuit-breaker trip
Load test: 10k qps synthetic traffic with mixed route labels to validate selective shedding behavior
E2E regression test gating p95/p99 against baseline across 10k simulated users
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Hedging increases token-usage/cost. Mitigation: single hedge only, cancel early, and cap hedges per route per minute; measure cost trade-offs in dashboard
Risk: Incorrect scoring weights can cause oscillation. Mitigation: start conservative locality_boost and deploy decay windows, enable rate-limiters on route flips

Risk: Shedding may impact enterprise customers unexpectedly. Mitigation: tie shedding policies to customer-tier labels and exclude enterprise routes by default; explicit opt-in required to shed premium routes
Risk: Telemetry/observability gap. Mitigation: add verbose logs in canary and create alerting rules for shed spikes
